subject: SOC 2 Type II window, SIG evidence, and EU/UK hosting attestation
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finserve.co.uk>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-29T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: FinServe compliance pack — SOC2 window + SIG/CAIQ ask

Hi Irene / Ben,

Quick one from our security team as we prepare the procurement packet: can you confirm whether Redwood's most recent SOC 2 Type II report covers the period that overlaps our audit window (we're looking for coverage for 01-JUL-2026 through 30-JUN-2027)? If not, would you be able to provide a bridge letter that attests to controls in the period between the report end and contract start?

In addition, they want the latest SIG matrix or CAIQ, and a short attestation on hosting: specifically, for EU customers can you confirm where inference data is processed/stored (region names are fine), whether the control plane or metadata crosses into non-EU jurisdictions, and whether you provide SCCs or equivalent for cross-border transfers. Also: KMS/HSM coverage for hosted customers vs. Dedicated/Private — is BYOK available?

Can you share the SOC2 (redacted is fine), a bridge letter template if available, and the SIG/CAIQ? We need these artifacts in the next 7 business days.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Liam
Information Security, FinServe Bank
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finserve.co.uk>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-29T11:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: FinServe compliance pack — SOC2 window + SIG/CAIQ ask

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front:
- We have a SOC 2 Type II report that covers 2026-11-01 through 2027-10-31 (I will attach the redacted PDF).
- We can issue a bridge letter to cover any audit window not fully contained in that period — we typically provide an interim attestation for the gap between the report end and contract start.
- We will send the SIG matrix (redacted rows ok) and a CAIQ link.
- Hosting: for hosted customers who select an EU region, inference processing stays in EU regions (we commonly use eu-west-1 / eu-central-1); control-plane metadata is routed through an EU control plane for EU-hosted tenants (details below). SCCs / UK Addendum options are supported for EU/UK customers.
- KMS: Dedicated and Private customers can use BYOK (customer-managed keys). Hosted customers can opt into a customer-managed KMS for enterprise plans; otherwise we use provider-managed keys with documented controls.

I'll loop in Neha from Security for the formal attestation and the bridge letter wording. Attaching timeline: will aim to get the SOC2 PDF + SIG + bridge letter draft over in 3 business days. Any specific redaction rules FinServe needs, call those out now (PII removal, example tenants, etc.).

Best,
Irene
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-11-01T09:20:00-05:00

Folks — forwarding FinServe's request (below). They asked for: the SOC2 Type II, a bridge letter if needed to cover their audit window, SIG/CAIQ, and a short attestation on EU/UK hosting + KMS.

Key questions for you, Neha:
- Confirm the SOC2 report period we should attach (I have 2026-11-01 to 2027-10-31).
- Can Security produce a bridge letter that attests to controls continuity from 2027-11-01 back to the report end, if the customer needs that? (they may need coverage for parts of 2027).
- Hosting / control plane: can you confirm which infra regions we can commit to for hosted EU customers, and whether any telemetry/metadata may route via a non-EU region for control-plane reasons (we need a clear yes/no + short note).
- KMS: wording for hosted customers (enterprise-level BYOK availability) and a short blurb for Dedicated/Private.

FinServe asked for artifacts within 7 business days — pinging since this is time sensitive for the deal.

Thanks — Irene

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finserve.co.uk>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-03T16:05:00+00:00
Subject: Re: FinServe compliance pack — SOC2 window + SIG/CAIQ ask

Hi Liam / Olivia — thanks for the patience. Per Irene's note, attaching the artifacts and summarizing answers to the specific asks below.

Attachments included (redacted where indicated):
- Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2027.pdf (redacted for customer tenant names; covers controls tested and sample population) — Scope: data processing and inference service controls.
- Redwood_Bridge_Letter_EU-UK_2027.docx (draft) — this provides an interim attestation for a requested period outside the Type II report coverage.
- SIG_matrix_finserve.xlsx — vendor self-assessment (some sections redacted for internal tooling details).

Summary answers and attestations:
1) SOC2 period coverage
   - The attached SOC 2 Type II report covers the period 2026-11-01 through 2027-10-31 (inclusive).
   - If your audit window requires coverage outside that span, we can issue a bridge letter attesting control continuity for the specified dates; see attached draft.

2) Bridge letter availability
   - Yes, we can provide a signed bridge letter. Typical turnaround is 48–72 business hours after security sign-off and any contract/legal approvals. The bridge letter language can be adapted to reference your audit window precisely.

3) Hosting / data residency and control plane
   - For EU-hosted tenants, inference processing and customer data at rest are kept in EU regions (we commonly use AWS eu-west-1 (Ireland) and eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) depending on customer region selection and availability).
   - We operate an EU-resident control plane for customers who select EU-hosting; in those configurations metadata and control-plane traffic remain in EU regions. We will provide a short technical diagram in a follow-up that maps data flows.
   - Where customers require contractual guarantees, we support SCCs (Standard Contractual Clauses) and the UK Addendum for cross-border transfers; we can include specific DPA language in the contract.

4) KMS / encryption
   - Dedicated and Private deployments: BYOK (customer-managed keys) is supported and recommended for full key control and HSM integration.
   - Hosted (standard): we use provider-managed keys by default, with documented operational controls. For enterprise-hosted customers (and Dedicated), we support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS (BYOK).

5) SIG / CAIQ and redaction guidance
   - SIG matrix attached; CAIQ link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=redwood/CAIQ-2027 (we provided a CAIQ export for your vendor assessment team).
   - If you need additional redactions, tell us which categories and we will produce a further redacted export.

Next steps
- If this looks good, please confirm the exact audit window dates you want the bridge letter to cover (if any).
- If you need a signed bridge letter now, we will route the attached draft through Legal and Security for signature — expected 2–4 business days.
- I can also share a short diagram mapping EU data flow and control-plane endpoints; let me know if you prefer AWS region names or cloud-provider-neutral wording.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2027.pdf (redacted), Redwood_Bridge_Letter_EU-UK_2027.docx (draft), SIG_matrix_finserve.xlsx
